title: Rapid attach: parameter pinning + KV cache prober for cold-snap mitigation
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Dedicated fleets experience intermittent ‘cold-snap’ events when tenant traffic shifts cause a node to start serving new model parameter slices while KV cache entries are cold. These events increase tail latency and reduce guaranteed throughput during bursts.

Goal: Implement a low-cost, tenant-aware rapid-attach mechanism that reduces cold-start overhead by (1) pinning critical parameter slices into memory on attach, (2) performing a prioritized KV cache probe and lightweight priming of the most frequently-accessed KV entries, and (3) integrating admission and autoscaling signals so the system keeps throughput guarantees without over-provisioning. The solution must be safe for multi-tenant fleets and runnable on Dedicated capacity with minimal regressions to memory fragmentation and eviction behavior.
acceptance_criteria: P95 tail latency for attach-workloads reduces by >= 40% compared to baseline cold attach in the staged perf test
Throughput under SLA load remains at or above committed tokens/sec for configured fleet sizes during attach spikes
Memory residency overhead per tenant on typical L model is < 12% compared to baseline after pinning policy
No increased error rate or OOM incidents in 72h canary on a subset of Dedicated fleet hosts
Feature gated behind runtime flag and telemetry produces attach-duration, kv-hit-rate, and pin-eviction metrics
tasks: Design spec: parameter pinning lifecycle, eviction penalty model, and KV probe prioritization (owner: Maya)
Prototype daemon: async background pinner + probe worker using existing weight-streaming API (owner: Oscar)
Benchmark harness: create synthetic attach spike workload with tenant churn and measure p95/p99 (owner: Perf eng)
Autoscaler integration: extend admission controller to consult pinning and kv-probe state before scaling decisions (owner: Infra)
Canary rollout: small Dedicated fleet region with feature flag and extended telemetry (owner: SRE)
Docs + runbook: explain knob settings, cost/benefit tradeoffs, and rollback steps (owner: Docs)
Code review and safety audit: ensure no blocking synchronous IO on request path (owner: Security)
Dashboard: per-tenant attach duration, kv-probe cost, memory overhead, and eviction rate (owner: Observability)
Cleanup: remove experimental debug flags after stabilization (owner: Oscar)
Postmortem template: collect data and decide default pinning policy for GA (owner: Maya)
decisions: Avoid full-model eager load: pin only hot slices and embed a progressive soft-pin that decays over time to avoid long-term residency growth
KV probe will be prioritized by recent token-access heatmaps computed from per-tenant traces, not by naive prefix frequency
Use asynchronous pre-warm worker that runs under admission-rate budget; synchronous prefetch on request path is disallowed
Expose two tuned policies: 'aggressive' for SLA-backed tenants (higher memory cost) and 'default' for best-effort tenants
Autoscaler will treat active pin budget as a soft constraint when deciding to burst scale; hard scaling still available for large sustained load
